intent: A founding story told as a sea voyage: the small host country lifts into colour, the brand-new stadium is pinned, and a ship draws the last leg of the Atlantic crossing down the coast to the river mouth, Brazil's squad aboard, before a flash marks the first final the hosts won.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Where was the FIRST FIFA World Cup played?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Where was the first FIFA World Cup played?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Uruguay. The very first World Cup, played in a single city, by 13 teams.

lines.direction: ease back over the River Plate; the Italian flag-ball thinks on 'Italy'; a trophy sticker on 'Brazil'; a house sticker on 'home' as Uruguay pulses
lines.text: Italy hosted the second. Brazil has won the most. But the first trophy stayed at home.

lines.direction: tighten on the capital; a medal sticker on 'champions'; the Montevideo pin and the Centenario tag on 'stadium'; a hammer sticker on 'opening' as Uruguay pulses
lines.text: The hosts were Olympic champions, and built a new stadium for it, finished days after the opening match.

lines.direction: pull far back up the Atlantic coast; the Rio pin on 'aboard' as the ship's last leg draws down the coast to the river mouth with a ship sticker riding it; a white flash and the 4–2 card on 'final' as the Uruguayan flag-ball grins and Uruguay pulses; the pins leave at the end
lines.text: Few European teams made the long voyage, and Brazil's squad climbed aboard on the way. In the final, the hosts beat Argentina.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: The first cup never left home. Follow us.
